newsitem.title: KENYA: CRICKET-AFRIDI SMASHES FASTEST ONE-DAY INTERNATIONAL CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AFRIDI SMASHES FASTEST ONE-DAY INTERNATIONAL CENTURY.

text.p: Pakistan 16-year-old all-rounder Shahid Afridi blasted the fastest one-day international century off 37 balls on Friday but his team only just scraped into the four-nations tournament final.
Afridi's 102 and incisive fast bowling from Waqar Younis, who captured five for 52, spurred Pakistan to an 82-run victory over Sri Lanka in the 50 overs round-robin match.

Yet if Sri Lanka had scored one more run -- they made 289 in reply to Pakistan's 371 for nine -- the World Cup winners would have qualified ahead of the Pakistanis on run rate for Sunday's final against South Africa.

Afridi's record-breaking performance transcended all else in the game after he was promoted to number three to boost the run rate and pulverised the bowling in an innings containing 11 sixes and six fours.

Playing in only his second limited overs international after his debut against Kenya on Tuesday, Afridi missed the fastest one-day international half-century by one ball, but beat the previous century record by 11 deliveries.
Both previous marks were held by Sri Lanka's dynamic opener Sanath Jayasuriya, who made 50 from 17 balls and 100 from 48 against Pakistan in the Singer Cup tournament in Singapore last April.

Afridi had the satisfaction of hammering Jayasuriya out of the attack, taking 43 off the left arm spinner's two overs, including five sixes. Afridi equalled Jayasuriya's record of 11 sixes in an innings.
Afridi, who came in at 60 for one, shared a second wicket partnership of 126 with his captain Saeed Anwar, who made sure his goodwork was not wasted with a classic 115.
Pakistan's 371 for nine beat their previous highest one-day international total of 338 for five against Sri Lanka in the 1983 World Cup at Swansea.
The previous highest one-day internaional match aggregate of 652 by Sri Lanka and Kenya in the World Cup on the sub-continent earlier this year was beaten by the 660 aggregate here.

Despite facing a daunting target, Sri Lanka's hopes soared with a brilliant 122 from Aravinda de Silva, and the match came to a compelling climax with 11 needed off Waqar's last over to secure a place in the final on run rate.
Left-arm seamer Chaminda Vaas heaved the first ball for six and the fourth for four, but Waqar's trademark yorker uprooted his stumps off the penultimate ball.
Sri Lanka had earlier been rocked by Waqar as he took four wickets in his first three overs.
A superb fifth wicket stand of 124 in 92 balls between de Silva and Arjuna Ranatunga raised Sri Lankan hopes of reaching the 290 needed to qualify on run rate.

When Ranatunga fell for 52, de Silva found another valuable ally in Kumar Dharmasena and the pair added 110 for the seventh wicket. But with the score at 270, de Silva aimed a wild heave at off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq and was stumped for 122 off 116 bals with 12 fours and two sixes.
When Dharmasena fell for 51 in the 49th over Sri Lanka panicked.
Muttiah Muralitheran perished to his first ball, another stumping victim off Saqlain, who finished with four for 33, before Waqar decisively cut short Vaas's threatening effort.
